doc.title: Josephine Davies interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 14, 2025

title: Her father's and mother's reactions to her music
summary: Her father dislikes what she plays, perhaps from his own unrealized rock and roll ambitions; her mother, a writer and poet, supports her and performed with her.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay last question, this is really deep. Did your dad ever come out to see you and what did he think? © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

I’ve got two answers for you. The first one is not really. My dad doesn’t like – well he likes a bit of trad jazz and he doesn’t like what I do even though he values the fact that I do something which requires a certain amount of skill and discipline. And I think there’s also an element of jealousy or slight envy because I think he really wanted to be a rock & roll pianist and didn’t, he didn’t do that. So I think he’s slightly frustrated as a performer himself. So no, he doesn’t come to see me play. But the other part of the answer is that my mum absolutely comes to everything. She’s a huge supporter and fan. And we did a gig together the other day. She’s a writer and a poet and so the band I’m recording with today actually, we did some free improvisation underneath and around a short story that she was reading and it was magical, really wonderful.
